provenance_note: The corpus was authored by another agent from the public specification and the cited standards with no access to this code; every ref in it is re-evaluated here against the shipping build, and no stored result is reused.
reference: Hand-built functional descriptions covering the four presets of SPEC-functionaldescription.md section 9, a clean baseline, and at least one trigger and one near-miss for each of the 71 rules FUN-R-001..094: id and tag normalisation and uniqueness, the condition grammar of section 3.6 with its unspaced tokenisation and unit compatibility, reference resolution, the reachability fixpoint of section 4.2 (including its worked example, whose synchronising transition a plain breadth-first walk would get wrong), dead ends and terminal steps, the satisfiability and overlap enumeration of section 4.3 with its variable order, sample points, rising/falling-edge constraints, the 65 536 cap at both sides of the boundary and the first-found witness, action qualifiers and their durations, set/reset pairing across sequences, operating-mode arbitration and the mode reachability of section 4.4 including the fault-response edge, loop tags, setpoint and setpoint-limit bounds with every stated equality boundary, fail positions against the I/O fail state, interlock and permissive references, alarm limits, ordering, priority, units and the skip clause of section 5.6, tag conventions, FD-versus-I/O conflicts, the known-tag set and range precedence with and without an I/O snapshot, unit conversion by section 3.8, the span arithmetic of section 4.5, and the written control_functions items and refusal reasons of section 7.4. Expected values were written from the specification text and then computed with an own standard-library engine (functionaldescription-ref.py) that implements sections 3.6, 4.1-4.5, 5, 6 and 7.4 independently; that engine reproduces every figure the specification states for its four presets - finding sets, counts, verdicts, reachable and unreachable lists, overlap witnesses, span percentages and the FN- item ids - which is the corpus's own check on itself. Standards clauses are cited as the specification cites them; the corpus author verified the clause numbering and titles of IEC 60848:2013 and IEC 62682:2022 against the publishers' preview documents and did not obtain the clause bodies of IEC 61131-3:2013 or ANSI/ISA-5.1-2024. Adjudication on 2026-09-23 corrected two expectations (the reachability list of r001-duplicate-ids and the FUN-R-093 finding of r003-parse-unit-and-mode-step-reference) and added four package cases covering the three spec 7.1 actions the corpus had left ungraded and the composition of the written register; each addition is marked in its own notes field. A second adjudication pass on 2026-09-23 added twelve cases against coverage holes rather than disagreements: the tool and this corpus agreed on all 94 earlier cases and all 1008 earlier checks. Each hole was demonstrated with a mutant of the tool that passes every one of those 94 cases; twenty-three such mutants are listed in ADJUDICATION.md, and each added case fails exactly the mutants of its own hole.

IEC 60848:2013 Edition 3.0, GRAFCET specification language for sequential function charts. Clause numbering and titles verified by the corpus author against the IEC preview PDF (cdn.standards.iteh.ai sample 19077): 3.1.1 Action, 3.1.11 Transition-condition, 3.1.13 Input variable, 3.1.14 Output variable, 3.1.15 Internal variable, 4.3.2 Structure, 4.3.3 Elements for interpretation, 4.4 Syntax rule, 4.5.2 Initial situation, 4.5.3 Clearing of a transition, 4.5.5 Simultaneous evolutions, 4.8.2 Continuous mode, 4.8.3 Stored mode, 4.10.5 Possible conflict on the value of the outputs, 6.2.3 Selection of sequences, 6.3.2 End of a sequence by a pit step, Annex B Figures B.5/B.6 structuring with operating modes. Two sentences were read in the preview and are quoted here: 4.3.3 "Associated with each transition, the transition-condition is a logical expression which is true or false and which is composed of input variables and/or internal variables" (basis of FUN-R-021) and 4.4 "Step transition and transition step alternation shall always be respected whatever the sequence". Basis of FUN-R-019, 021, 027, 028, 052, 071.

Basis of FUN-R-011, 012, 013, 017, 022, 023, 024, 025.

TZ-engineering-workflow.md section 2 (_docs/TZ-engineering-workflow.md): the control_functions register belongs to functionaldescription with the FN- id prefix and carries system_id, mode, sequence steps, setpoints in SI, interlock references and the io tags referenced - the basis of FUN-R-007 and of the section 7.4 item fields.

tolerance: Finding sets (keyed rule@target, with #tag where section 5 says "per tag"), severities, severity counts, verdicts, tag_source, initial/reachable/unreachable/dead-end id lists, overlap a/b/resolved, mode reachability lists, range_source, written item ids and their id/fd_id/kind/label/mode_ids/io_tags/interlock_refs, the ids and order of the control_functions array a save produces, the ignored reason-to-count map of a load, and the package refusal reason: exact, because every one of them is a discrete outcome of a boolean or set-theoretic condition of the specification, with no arithmetic between the input and the answer. Instrument ranges are exact: they are the stored bounds copied through section 4.1. sp_span_pct and limit_span_pct: relative 1e-12, absolute 0 when the reference is 0, because section 4.5 fixes the expression (value - a) / (b - a) x 100 and the same three binary64 operations run in the same order on both sides; the references keep the full binary64 repr, so 16.666666666666664 and -12.500000000000005 are reproduced digit for digit rather than rounded. Overlap witnesses: booleans exact; numbers relative 1e-12, since a witness value is either a stated threshold, a threshold plus or minus 1, or the binary64 midpoint (t_i + t_i+1) / 2 of two thresholds. Setpoint values written to the package: relative 1e-12, one copy of a stored SI value. No tolerance here was chosen to let an implementation pass: each is the arithmetic width of the operation the specification names, and every categorical answer is graded at zero width.

not_benchmarked: Figure geometry, colours, truncation and the layout rules of spec 10: presentation, with no reference to compute (spec 14). The countable figure properties of spec 13 (one box per step, one bar per transition, unreachable steps marked, one node per mode and one arrow per exit) are derivable from the graded step, transition and mode lists but need the rendered DOM, so they are left to the QA harness.
Finding and headline wording and its seven translations: language QA covers them (spec 14). The corpus grades rule, target, tag and severity only.
Report profile of spec 11, PDF output and the report gates of AGENTS section 8.
Permalink round-trip and the 4 000-character io-dropping rule (spec 15.9): a UI budget.
Run-time behaviour: mode arbitration in the plant, SFC scan timing, and whether a reported overlap can physically occur - the model treats tags as independent (spec 2.1, 2.3, 14).

Package reading, the part of spec 7.1-7.3 with no result to compare: the system and package pickers, the conflict display of TZ-project-package 3.4, and the flags display of spec 7.5. The four actions themselves are graded through the spec 13 harness window.__functionaldescriptionPackage, which takes the package document as an argument and needs no live DiagramProject runtime: load_io in pkg-load-io-mapping, open_fd:<code> in pkg-open-fd-round-trip, apply_project in pkg-apply-project-touches-no-other-section and save in the four write cases. The ignored lists are graded as a reason-to-count map; the byte-identical carry-over of other fd_id items and of unknown-kind items is graded by their ids and order in pkg-save-keeps-other-codes-and-unknown-kinds, not byte by byte.
Purity and idempotence of window.__functionaldescriptionAnalyse (acceptance criterion 3) and the 390 px / 1440 px layout criteria: properties of the harness and the page, not of a case.
The Python export file and its self-test (spec 12): the quantities it covers are graded here through the same case outputs.
The entry limits of spec 3.12 (400 tags, 60 steps, 300 characters per condition and so on): input is refused at entry with a message, which is a UI behaviour and produces no result object to compare.

The 65 536 cap is graded at N = 65 536 and N = 131 072. N = 65 537 exactly, named in acceptance criterion 5, is not constructible: 65 537 is the Fermat prime 2^16 + 1, so P(2k_v + 1) x 2^b = 65 537 forces b = 0 and a single numeric operand with 32 768 distinct thresholds, which the 300-character condition limit of spec 3.12 forbids. The corpus grades the inequality at the two nearest realisable points instead.

Finding order. Spec 6 orders findings by severity, then rule id, then target in state order, but spec 13 grades findings as a set of (rule, target, tag), so no case can see the order. Nine mutants of the comparator pass all 106 cases. The order is a report property and is checked by the site report gates, not here.

coverage.summary: 106 cases: the 4 presets of spec 9, a clean baseline, an empty model, 75 rule and boundary cases covering all 71 rule ids FUN-R-001..094 with a trigger and a near-miss each, 5 derived-quantity cases (known-tag set and range precedence, unit conversion, two span-arithmetic cases, parallel divergence), 11 coverage cases added by the second adjudication pass of 2026-09-23 (alarm type DEV against the FUN-R-086 set and the HH/H/L/LL range rules; the "entry non-empty" conjunct of the spec 4.4 global_entry seed; the direction and unit branches of FUN-R-092; the P and L first letters of FUN-R-091; the keyword arm of the spec 3.1 tag rule; the three FUN-R-084 comparisons at exact equality; the =, <>, < and <= comparisons, the step-time sample point at 0, the bare numeric reference and the RE/FE constraints of spec 4.3; the bus direction field of spec 3.3 against FUN-R-027; the empty-to arm of FUN-R-004; FUN-R-011 at exactly one step; and the min < max guard on the I/O range of spec 4.1), and 9 package cases: four on the write path of spec 7.4 (one full write and the three refusal reasons, with a fourth refusal case for a non-empty malformed code), one on the composition of the written register, and one on each of the other three spec 7.1 actions (load_io, open_fd:<code>, apply_project). Every expected value of the first 94 cases was computed with functionaldescription-ref.py, which reproduces every figure spec 9 states for its four presets; the 12 cases added by adjudication were computed from the specification text by the adjudicator and are marked in their own notes fields.
ambiguities: Spec 4.3.5 states N = P(2k_v + 1) x 2^b while spec 4.3.2 drops negative sample points for a step time, so the enumerated domain can be smaller than N. The corpus computes the cap guard from the stated formula and keeps both cap cases free of step-time variables, where the two readings agree.

The spec 5 preamble "A rule whose inputs are invalid (a blocker on the same field) is not evaluated on that field" is not itemised. The corpus reads it as: a condition that fails FUN-R-003 is excluded from FUN-R-016/017/018/020/021/094; an action whose qualifier fails FUN-R-008 is excluded from FUN-R-022/023/024/025; an alarm whose type fails FUN-R-008 is excluded from the range rules; an element whose id fails FUN-R-002 still gets its other rules. Case r008-enum-violations grades that reading. Spec 5 carries this itemisation as changelog line C3 of 2026-09-23; it also settles that a FUN-R-006 blocker on duration_s, on_delay_s, off_delay_s or deadband suppresses nothing, and that a FUN-R-002 blocker on an id or tag suppresses nothing.

Whether a step reference to an unknown step (FUN-R-004) makes a transition condition "not evaluable" for the pair enumeration of spec 4.3 is not stated. The corpus treats it as not evaluable, so transition T4 of r004-unknown-references forms no pair with T0 although they share step S0. A reading that keeps such a condition evaluable would add one FUN-R-017 there. Adjudication on 2026-09-23 settled this on spec 3.6, whose step-reference bullet reads "IDENT shall be a step of the same sequence (else FUN-R-004)": a reference that names no step of the sequence denotes no quantity, so the condition is not evaluable and the pair is not examined. Spec 4.3 carries the resolution as changelog line C6. The corpus reading stands and r004-unknown-references is unchanged.
FUN-R-092's range tolerance "|D| > 1e-9 x max(1, |value|)" does not say which of the two values. The corpus uses the I/O value; every case differs by 10 K, far outside either reading.
Spec 3.6 says keywords are case-insensitive but says nothing about UNIT tokens. The corpus matches them case-sensitively, which is the only way degC, Pa, kPa and MPa stay distinct.

FUN-R-060 tests "unit(pv) known". The corpus reads that as attr(pv) resolving at all, including a digital tag whose unit is the empty string; no case pairs a digital PV with a non-empty sp.unit, so the alternative reading changes nothing here.

Spec 3.4 says fault_response is present only when target or description is non-empty, while FUN-R-033 defines a trigger for an object whose two fields are both blank. The corpus grades the FUN-R-033 reading in r033-blank-fault-response-counts-as-none.
FUN-R-028 targets "the second such action": read as the second action on that tag inside the step, by action index.

FUN-R-084 says "one per violating pair", but spec 13 grades findings as a set of (rule, target, tag) and the rule carries no tag, so two violating pairs that target the same alarm collapse into one entry. r084-limit-ordering-violations has one violating pair per target, so the two readings agree there.
Spec 5.6 skips the range rules "when FUN-R-086 fires". FUN-R-084 compares two alarms; the corpus skips a pair when either of its alarms fired FUN-R-086.

Spec 13 lists the package refusal reasons collision, invalid_id and no_code while spec 7.4 names the refusing conditions as FUN-R-001, FUN-R-002, FUN-R-007 and an id collision. The corpus maps an empty code to no_code and a duplicate or malformed element id to invalid_id, and grades no case where fd.code is non-empty but malformed, because that could reasonably carry either reason. Adjudication on 2026-09-23 settled this on the one-to-one correspondence between the three refusing conditions of spec 7.4 (FUN-R-007 on fd.code, FUN-R-001/002 on element ids and tags, an id collision) and the three reasons of spec 13 (no_code, invalid_id, collision): FUN-R-007 is the only one that reads fd.code and it covers both the empty and the malformed arm, so a malformed non-empty code refuses with no_code. Spec 7.4 carries the resolution as changelog line C7, and pkg-refused-malformed-code now grades it.
Spec 7.4 says io_tags are "the tags the element references"; for a condition that does not parse no tag can be read out of it. Every package case here uses conditions that parse.

A duplicated element id (FUN-R-001) leaves two array entries. Spec 4.2 builds R with set operations, so the reachability lists carry each step id once however many rows share it; an earlier reference for r001-duplicate-ids listed S1 twice and was corrected by adjudication on 2026-09-23. Spec 4.2 carries the resolution as changelog line C1.

Whether a condition that parses but fails the unit-compatibility test of spec 3.6 still contributes its IDENTs as tag references was disputed for r003-parse-unit-and-mode-step-reference. Adjudication on 2026-09-23 settled it on the last bullet of spec 3.6 - every IDENT that is not a step reference is a tag reference - and on FUN-R-003 listing "does not parse" and "UNIT incompatible with its operand" as separate triggers: a condition that parses contributes its tags, one that does not parse contributes none. Spec 3.6 carries the resolution as changelog line C2.
